The '''2010–11 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team''' represented [[Georgetown University]] in the 2010–2011 [[NCAA Division I]] basketball season.  In November, the team played in and won the [[Charleston Classic]] tournament.<ref name=wpost>{{cite news|last=El-Bashir|first=Tarik|title=Georgetown men's basketball defeats N.C. State to win Charleston Classic|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/11/21/AR2010112104607.html|access-date=February 8, 2011|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=November 22, 2010}}</ref> During the February 23 game against the [[2010–11 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati Bearcats]], senior [[Chris Wright (basketball, born 1989)|Chris Wright]] injured his hand, and later had surgery that kept him out of the final conference games. Without him, the Hoyas lost in their first game in the [[2011 Big East men's basketball tournament]]. The team ultimately received an at-large invitation as a 6 seed in the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]],<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.washingtonpost.com/ncaa-tournament-georgetown-to-face-either-vcu-or-usc/2011/03/11/ABVEHDU_story.html |title= NCAA tournament: Georgetown to face either VCU or USC |work=The Washington Post |first= Tarik |last= El-Bashir |date= March 13, 2011 |access-date=March 14, 2011}}</ref> where they lost in the second round to [[2010–11 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU.]] They finished the season 21–11, 10–8 in Big East play.

==Previous season==
{{2010–11 Big East men's basketball standings}}
In their [[2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|previous season]], the team finished the season 23–11, and 10–8 in Big East play, and advanced to the championship game of the [[2010 Big East men's basketball tournament]]. Sophomore [[Greg Monroe]] declined to return, and entered the NBA draft where he was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]].

==Season recap==
Although star [[Center (basketball)|center]] [[Greg Monroe]] had opted to forego his senior year of college and enter the [[2010 NBA draft|2010 National Basketball Association draft]] after the end of [[2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the previous season]] and reserve [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] Stephan Stepka had transferred to [[James Madison Dukes men's basketball|James Madison]], the Hoyas returned the rest of the core and reserve players of their 2009–10 team. Senior [[Julian Vaughn]] and sophomore [[Hollis Thompson]] at [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] and seniors [[Austin Freeman]] and [[Chris Wright (basketball, born 1989)|Chris Wright]] and sophomore [[Jason Clark (basketball)|Jason Clark]] at [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] all returned as starters or major contributors off the bench. Sophomore [[Vee Sanford]] also returned as a reserve guard, sophomore [[Jerrelle Benimon]] as a reserve forward, and junior [[Henry Sims]] as a reserve [[Center (basketball)|center]]. Freshmen joining the Hoyas for the season included guard [[Markel Starks]], who later would emerge as their [[point guard]], forwards Nate Lubick and Aaron Bowen, and center Moses Ayegba. Freshman guard John Caprio also made the team as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]]. Ranked No. 20 in the [[AP Poll|Associated Press Poll]] to start the season, Georgetown hoped for another successful campaign in 2010–2011, and to return to the NCAA tournament for the fifth time in six seasons. The Hoyas also hoped for a deeper run in the tournament, which they had exited in the first weekend of play in their last two appearances in [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2008]] and [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2010]].

===Non-conference schedule===

Georgetown began the season with six straight wins over unranked opponents. In their season opener, at [[2010–11 Old Dominion Monarchs basketball team|Old Dominion]], they broke the Monarchs′ 23-game home winning streak – the fourth-longest active streak in the [[United States]], dating back to January 2009 – behind 19 points by Chris Wright, 18 by Jason Clark, and 17 by Austin Freeman.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052947/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303160295 espn.com Anonymous, "Georgetown uses late rally to edge Old Dominion," Associated Press, November 13, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303160295 espn.com Georgetown vs. Old Dominion –  Box Score – November 12, 2010 – ESPN]</ref> Following a win in their home opener over [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane]] in which Freeman scored 23 points, Jason Clark had a [[double-double]] with 17 points and 11 rebounds, and Vee Sanford contributed 10 points off the bench,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202053118/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303190046 espn.com Anonymous, "Austin Freeman's 23 points help Georgetown hold off Tulane," Associated Press, November 16, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303190046 espn.com Tulane vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – November 15, 2010 – ESPN]</ref> the Hoyas traveled to [[Charleston, South Carolina|Charleston]], [[South Carolina]], to take part in the [[Charleston Classic]] as its only ranked team. As [[NASCAR]] driver and former Hoya player [[Brendan Gaughan]] looked on from the stands, they won the opener against [[2010–11 Coastal Carolina Chanticleers men's basketball team|Coastal Carolina]], with Clark scoring 22 points, Freeman scoring 20, and Chris Wright getting a double-double with 12 points and 12 rebounds.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202053020/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303220046 espn.com Anonymous, "Jason Clark leads 3-point barrage for Georgetown," Associated Press, November 18, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303220046 espn.com Coastal Carolina vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – November 18, 2010 – ESPN]</ref> They followed this with a semifinal win over [[2010–11 Wofford Terriers men's basketball team|Wofford]] in which Julian Vaughn had a double-double with 12 points and 10 rebounds, Chris Wright had a game-high 18 points, and Austin Freeman scored 14,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160804141727/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303232747 espn.com Anonymous, "Chris Wright leads Georgetown into final of Charleston Classic," Associated Press, November 19, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303232747 espn.com Georgetown vs. Wofford –  Box Score – November 19, 2010 – ESPN]</ref> and a victory in the final game over [[2010–11 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|North Carolina State]] to win the tournament. In the championship game, the Hoya starters had a balanced attack against the Wolfpack, with Hollis Thompson scoring a game-high 18 points, Wright 17, Freeman 15, and Clark 14.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202053034/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303250152 espn.com Anonymous, "Georgetown pulls away from North Carolina State to win Charleston Classic," Associated Press, November 22, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303250152 espn.com Georgetown vs. NC State –  Box Score – November 21, 2010 – ESPN]</ref> Ranked No. 16 in the AP Poll, the Hoyas then returned to the Verizon Center, where Freeman tied a school record shared by Mark Tillmon and Darrel Owens by hitting seven three-pointers, going 7-for-9 (77.7%) from three-point range, and scored 32 points in a win over [[2010–11 UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball team|UNC Asheville]]. Julian Vaughn scored 16 points against the Bulldogs, and Jason Clark had a double-double with 11 points and 10 rebounds.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052649/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303310046 espn.com Anonymous, "Austin Freeman 7 for 9 from 3-point range to lead 6–0 Georgetown," Associated Press, November 27, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303310046 espn.com UNC Asheville vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – November 27, 2010 – ESPN]</ref>

With a record of 6–0, Georgetown next faced its first ranked opponent of the season, unbeaten No. 9 [[2010–11 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]], in a game at the [[Sprint Center]] in [[Kansas City, Missouri|Kansas City]], [[Missouri]]. The Hoyas started strong, hitting seven of their first eight shots to take a 14–9 lead with 16:24 left in the first half. They then went on a 14–4 run to pull out to a 23–13 lead with 11:33 left in the half, and followed with a 9–0 run to stretch their lead to 35–17 with 8:53 left. Missouri followed with an 8–2 run of its own, but at the end of it Georgetown still led 38–25, having shot 15-for-19 (79.0%) from the field. At the half, Georgetown had shot 20-for-28 (71.4%) from the field and still led 54–47, but the Tigers were in the midst of a comeback that continued into the second half and, with 8:25 to left to play in regulation, took their first lead of the game, 77–75, on a three-pointer by junior guard [[Marcus Denmon]]. Vee Sanford responded with a three-pointer of his own that put the Hoyas back in front, 78–77, with 7:49 left. Sophomore point guard [[Michael Dixon (basketball)|Michael Dixon]] scored on a layup to take the lead back for Missouri, and the Tigers moved out to an 85–80 advantage with 4:21 to play. After a Georgetown timeout, Austin Freeman scored five consecutive points on a free throw and two layups to tie the game at 85–85 with 3:35 to go. The teams continued to trade baskets until Dixon sank two free throws with 26 seconds left to give Missouri a 93–89 lead. After Chris Wright also sank two free throws to close to 93–91, Dixon hit the first of two free throws to give Missouri a 94–91 lead with 14.1 seconds remaining in regulation, but missed the second, and Wright responded with a three-pointer with one second left that tied the game at 94–94 and forced overtime. In overtime, the score stood at 98–98 when Georgetown went on a 9–2 run thanks to Jason Clark – who until then had gone 1-for-6 from beyond the three-point line – hitting three straight three-pointers, giving the Hoyas a 107–100 lead with 1:22 remaining, and Georgetown hung on to secure a 111–102 upset overtime win and a 7–0 start for the second consecutive season. Austin Freeman scored 31 points, his second straight game with more than 30 points, while Jason Clark had 26, Chris Wright had a double-double with 21 points and 10 assists, and Henry Sims came off the bench to score 10 points. The Hoyas shot 18-for-18 from the free throw line and hit 15 three-pointers, and their 111 points were the most Missouri had allowed since a 111–56 defeat at the hands of [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] on January 3, 1998.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202102741/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303340142 espn.com Anonymous, "Georgetown tops Missouri in battle of ranked teams," Associated Press, December 1, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303310046 espn.com Georgetown vs. Missouri –  Box Score – November 30, 2010 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=303340142 espn.com Georgetown vs. Missouri –  Play-by-Play – November 30, 2010 – ESPN]</ref>

The Hoyas returned to the Verizon Center for a win over [[2010–11 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]] in which Chris Wright finished with a game-high 21 points and four steals, and Georgetown improved to 8–0 for the second straight season.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052705/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303380046 espn.com Anonymous, "Georgetown defense does trick vs. Utah State as long-range shooting sputters," Associated Press, December 4, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303380046 espn.com Utah States vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – December 4, 2010 – ESPN]</ref> By the time they visited [[2010–11 Temple Owls men's basketball team|Temple]] five days later, the Hoyas had risen to No. 9 in the AP Poll, but behind a 30-point performance by junior guard [[Ramone Moore]] Temple upset Georgetown to give Owls head coach [[Fran Dunphy]] his 400th career victory and end the Hoyas′ winning streak despite 15 points by Jason Clark, 14 each by Austin Freeman and Julian Vaughn, and 10 by Chris Wright.<ref>[http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId/303430218 Anonymous, "Ramone Moore scores 30 to lead Temple past No. 10 Georgetown," Associated Press, December 10, 2010.]{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303430218 espn.com Temple vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – December 9, 2010 – ESPN]</ref> Back at the Verizon Center, Georgetown had two easy wins, defeating first [[Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball|Appalachian State]] and then [[Loyola Greyhounds men's basketball|Loyola of Maryland]]. Jason Clark finished with 15 points and Austin Freeman with 14 against Appalachian States, while Nate Lubick and Hollis Thompson each scored 11 points and Chris Wright had 12 assists in the game. As two Georgetown students wearing biblical clothing and long false beards held up a "Free Moses" sign, freshman center Moses Ayegba – ruled ineligible for Georgetown's first nine games because he had received an airline ticket to the United States from his native [[Nigeria]] from a non-family member – made his collegiate debut in the Appalachian State game, scoring two points. Against Loyola six days later, Austin Freeman and Hollis Thompson each scored 14 points, Henry Sims contributed 12, and Chris Wright added 11.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202102732/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303460046 Anonymous, "Georgetown follows first loss with rout of overmatched Appalachian State," Associated Press, December 12, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303460046 espn.com Appalachian State vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – December 12, 2010 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052912/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303520046 Anonymous, "Georgetown shakes off exam-week concerns, trounces Loyola of Maryland," Associated Press, December 18, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303520046 espn.com Loyola (MD) vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – December 18, 2010 – ESPN]</ref>

Falling to No. 15 in the AP Poll by the time of the Loyola game, Georgetown rose again to No. 10 by the time it rounded out its non-conference schedule with a visit to No. 16 [[2010–11 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]], its second ranked opponent of the season. From the field, the Hoyas shot 52 percent in the first half, 63 percent in the second half, and 57 percent for the game, committing only six turnovers, and emerged as the second-best shooting team in the United States in field goal percentage for the season at 52.5 percent. Georgetown held an early lead, but the game remained close, and Memphis took the lead at 15–14 with 13:30 remaining in the first half. The Tigers extended this to their largest lead of the game, 22–18, with 10:00 until halftime, but the Hoyas regained the advantage at 24–22 with 8:41 to play in the half and never trailed again. Leading 40–36 at halftime, the Hoyas pulled away in the second half, leading 76–59 with 3:37 left in the game and winning 89–69. Austin Freeman led the team with a game-high 24 points, while Chris Wright added 19 and Julian Vaughn had a double-double with 15 points and 10 rebounds.<ref>[http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId/303570235 Anonymous, "No. 9 Georgetown pulls away in second half to win at No. 17 Memphis," Associated Press, December 24, 2010.]{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303570235 espn.com Georgetown vs. Memphis –  Box Score – December 23, 2010 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=303570235 espn.com Georgetown vs. Memphis –  Play-by-Play – December 23, 2010 – ESPN]</ref>

===Conference schedule===

The 11–1 Hoyas were back to No. 9 in the AP Poll when they began their Big East season on December 29 with their second straight road game against a ranked opponent, facing No. 15 [[2010–11 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]] at [[South Bend, Indiana|South Bend]], [[Indiana]]. The Hoyas entered the game as the fourth-best three-point-shooting team in the United States, but a strong defensive effort by the underdog Fighting Irish held Georgetown to only 4-for-22 (18.2%) from three-point range and also limited the offensive output of Chris Wright (3 points) and Jason Clark (8 points); Austin Freeman had a 21-point game, but as a team Georgetown shot only 42.6 percent from the field. The Fighting Irish also enjoyed a big advantage from the free-throw line, going 22-for-27 to the Hoyas′ 5-for-9. The game was close for about the first 10 minutes, but then the Fighting Irish went on an 8–0 run that gave them the lead for good at 23–15 with 7:35 left until halftime. In the second half, a 14–2 Fighting Irish run gave Notre Dame a 48–32 lead with 11:55 left in the game. The Hoyas responded with a 9–0 run of their own that closed the gap to 48–41 with 8:16 left, but two Fighting Irish three-pointers followed that pushed their lead to 56–43. A layup and two free throws by Freeman got the Hoyas′ deficit to single digits at 56–47 with 3:53 to play, but Notre Dame then extended its lead again and upset the Hoyas, winning 69–55. It was the first time that Georgetown had lost its Big East opener during John Thompson III's tenure, breaking a 7–0 Georgetown winning streak in conference openers since Thompson's first season with the team [[2004-05 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2004–05]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052946/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303630087 Anonymous, "Tim Abromaitis helps Notre Dame upset Georgetown," Associated Press, December 29, 2010.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=303630087 espn.com Georgetown vs. Notre Dame –  Box Score – December 29, 2010 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=303630087 espn.com Georgetown vs. Notre Dame –  Play-by-Play – December 29, 2010 – ESPN]</ref>

Returning to Washington to play their first [[New Year's Day]] game since [[1942-43 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1943]], the Hoyas defeated the Big East's weakest team, [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]], in DePaul's first New Year's Day game since at least 1945 and dealt the Blue Demons their 10th consecutive loss to Georgetown, 15th consecutive loss to a Big East opponent, and 25th consecutive road loss, with Austin Freeman and Jason Clark each scoring 21 points, Chris Wright emerging in the second half from a shooting slump to contribute 17, and Julian Vaughn pulling down 10 rebounds and adding nine points.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202053024/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310010046 Anonymous, "Austin Freeman, Jason Clark score 21 each for Georgetown," Associated Press, January 1, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310010046 espn.com DePaul vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – January 1, 2011 – ESPN]</ref> The season then took its first real downturn. Falling to No. 13 in the AP Poll after the win over DePaul, the Hoyas lost first at [[Madison Square Garden]] to [[2010–11 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]] in the last few seconds of a close game in which Hollis Thompson scored 16 points but Clark, Freeman, and Wright combined for only 20, and then at the Verizon Center to [[2010–11 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]], with Clark scoring 16 and Freeman 11 but the Mountaineers making up for poor shooting by dominating in offensive rebounds (15–4) and free throw attempts (24–11) and forcing the Hoyas into 18 turnovers.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202102737/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310032599 Anonymous, "Justin Brownlee's basket with 10 seconds left helps St. John's upset Georgetown," Associated Press, January 4, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310032599 espn.com Georgetown vs. St. John's –  Box Score – January 3, 2011 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId/310080046 Anonymous, "Casey Mitchell scores 28 points as Mountaineers pressure Hoyas," Associated Press, January 8, 2011.]{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310080046 espn.com West Virginia vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – January 8, 2011 – ESPN]</ref>

Dropping to No. 22 in the AP Poll and, at 1–3 in conference play, off to its worst start in the Big East since the [[2003-04 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2003–04 season]] – [[Craig Esherick]]′s last as head coach – Georgetown next hosted No. 5 [[2010–11 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]], the winners of five straight games. The Hoyas never led in the game, and their slumping backcourt of Clark, Freeman, and Wright could not compete with the perimeter shooters of the Panthers. The Hoyas also slumped at the free-throw line, making only 4 of 14 foul shots (28.6%) in the first half – to the boos of the crowd – and 14 of 25 (56.0%) in the game. Freeman and Wright got in early foul trouble, and Pittsburgh jumped out to a 19–9 advantage with 10:54 remaining in the first half and led by double digits for the rest of the game. Wright and Freeman finally began to score in the second half, and Wright led the Hoyas with 14 points, while Julian Vaughn had 13 and Freeman scored 12. Georgetown never went on a run greater than 4–0 until late in the second half, when they scored seven unanswered points to cut Pittsburgh's lead from 18 to 11 points with 5:32 to play, but the Panthers pulled away again and cruised to a 72–57 victory. Although the Hoyas ended the game leading the Big East in field-goal percentage at 50.9%,<ref name=ap20110115>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202053022/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310150164 Anonymous, "Austin Freeman's 25 help send Georgetown past Rutgers, end skid at 3," Associated Press, January 15, 2011.]</ref> the loss was Georgetown's third in a row, and left them with a 1–4 Big East record, their worst start in the conference since [[1998-99 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1998–99]], the season in which [[John Thompson Jr.]] had resigned as head coach.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052713/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310120046 Anonymous, "Ashton Gibbs helps No. 5 Pittsburgh pull away from No. 19 Georgetown early," Associated Press, January 12, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310120046 espn.com Pittsburgh vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – January 12, 2011 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=310120046 espn.com Pittsburgh vs. Georgetown –  Play-by-Play – January 12, 2011 – ESPN]</ref>

After the Pittsburgh game, the Hoya backcourt pulled out of its slump, and a new winning streak began with victories at [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] – the Scarlet Knights' ninth loss in their previous 10 games against Georgetown – and [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] and in a rematch with St. John's at the Verizon Center, dealing each opponent its fifth loss in six games and, in the case of St. John's, extending the Red Storm's string of consecutive road losses against ranked teams to 32, dating back to 2002. Austin Freeman had 25 points and a career-high nine rebounds against Rutgers, 28 points at Seton Hall, and 14 points in the one-sided win over St. John's, while Chris Wright finished with 15 points at Rutgers and 17 at Seton Hall. Jason Clark scored 13 points at Rutgers and 16 against St. John's, while Hollis Thompson contributed 14 points at Seton Hall and 15 against St. John's. Julian Vaughn scored 11 at Seton Hall, and Nate Lubick made his first collegiate start in the St. John's game, committing four turnovers but scoring six points.<ref name=ap20110115/><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310150164 espn.com Georgetown vs. Rutgers –  Box Score – January 15, 2011 – ESPN]</ref><ref name=ap20110119>[http://mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId/310182550 Anonymous, "Hoyas shake off spirited Pirates run for second straight win," Associated Press, January 19, 2011.]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310182550 espn.com Georgetown vs. Seton Hall –  Box Score – January 18, 2011 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052917/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310260046 Anonymous, "Georgetown wins 3rd straight behind Hollis Thompson's 15," Associated Press, January 27, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310260046 espn.com St. John's vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – January 26, 2011 – ESPN]</ref> Georgetown entered the Seton Hall game with the third-highest team field-goal percentage in the United States, at 50.7 percent.<ref name=ap20110119/> The Hoyas dropped to No. 23 in the AP Poll before the Seton Hall game, but climbed to No. 21 in time for the game against St. John's, and the three wins evened their Big East record at 4–4.

Second in the United States in team field-goal percentage at 50.8 percent, the Hoyas next traveled to [[Philadelphia]], [[Pennsylvania]], to face No. 8 [[2010–11 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] at the [[Wells Fargo Center (Philadelphia)|Wells Fargo Center]]. Georgetown fell behind the Wildcats early, trailing 10–5 with 16:24 to play in the first half, but then came back to post a 32–26 lead at halftime. The Hoyas more or less held that lead until the Wildcats began a surge with 2:53 to play and closed to only a 61–60 deficit with 2:08 left. The Hoyas then got the ball to Austin Freeman repeatedly; he made a two-point layup to increase Georgetown's lead to 63–60 with 1:39 left, then, after Villanova sophomore guard [[Maalik Wayns]] made two free throws, hit a two-point jumper to extend Georgetown's lead to 65–62. After two more Wayns free throws, a dunk by Nate Lubick, and a layup by Wayns made the score Georgetown 67 Villanova 66, Freeman sank two free throws to secure a 69–66 upset victory for the Hoyas. Freeman went 8-for-8 in free throws and scored 10 of Georgetown's last 12 points on the way to a 30-point game, while Jason Clark scored 10 points, and Julian Vaughn went 7-for-7 from the free-throw line in a 9-point performance.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052837/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310290222 Anonymous, "Austin Freeman takes over in clutch as Georgetown upends Villanova," Associated Press, January 29, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310290222 espn.com Georgetown vs. Villanova –  Box Score – January 29, 2011 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=310290222 –  Play-by-Play – January 29, 2011 – ESPN]</ref><!--A play-by-play scoring error at 4:26 left in the first half displays Georgetown's score as two points lower than the actual score for the remainder of the play-by-play record.-->

With a winning conference record (5–4) for the first time in the season, Georgetown rose to No. 13 in the AP Poll and returned home to face No. 15 [[2010–11 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]], the Hoyas′ second ranked conference opponent in two days. Both teams had a lackluster first half; the Hoyas shot 31 percent from the field, the Cardinals shot 26 percent, the teams had a combined 12 turnovers before they scored a combined 12 points (on the way to having 16 turnovers each before the game was over) and at the half the score was Georgetown 22 Louisville 18. In the second half, however, the Georgetown offense came alive; the Hoyas went on a 10–2 run to take a 34–25 lead with 16:31 left to play, but the Cardinals went on a 15–4 run of their own to tie the game at 47–47 with 7:56 remaining. After that, the game remained tight, but the Hoyas shot 13-for-17 (76%) from the field in the second half and hung on to win 72–69, extending their winning streak to five games. Chris Wright, who had not scored a single point in the Villanova game, went 8-for-8 from in free throws and scored a game-high 24 against Louisville, including two free throws with five seconds left to help clinch the victory. Austin Freeman saw his streak of 23 consecutive free throws end but nonetheless had 13 points, and Julian Vaughn added 10.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052711/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310310046 Anonymous, "Chris Wright leads Hoyas to ugly win over Louisville," Associated Press, January 31, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310310046 espn.com Louisville vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – January 31, 2011 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=310310046 espn.com Georgetown vs. Villanova –  Play-by Play – January 31, 2011 – ESPN]</ref> Five days later, the Hoyas stretched their winning streak to six, holding off [[2010–11 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] despite a 43-point game – fifth-highest ever in a Big East game at the time – by Providence senior guard-forward [[Marshon Brooks]]. Freeman scored 23 points against the Friars, while Jason Clark contributed 18, Chris Wright added 16, and Julian Vaughn had a double-double with 14 points and a career-high 11 rebounds.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052737/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310360046 Anonymous, "Georgetown manages to win despite Marshon Brooks' 43 points for Providence," Associated Press, February 5, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310360046 espn.com Providence vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – February 5, 2011 – ESPN]</ref>

Georgetown was No. 11 in the AP Poll and ranked second in the United States in team field goal percentage at 50.5 percent when it went on the road for a game at No. 12 [[2010–11 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]], its third ranked conference opponent in four games. The Hoyas got out to a 16–10 lead halfway through the first half, but Syracuse responded with a 13–2 run, and at halftime the Orange led 31–29. Syracuse extended the lead to 37–31, but the Hoyas rallied to pull ahead 39–38. Then a key Syracuse player, senior forward [[Rick Jackson]], went to the bench with four fouls with 14:40 left to play, and the Orange had to play with three freshmen on the court. Georgetown extended its lead to 44–40, but Syracuse overcame Jackson's absence to battle its way back into the lead, and the Orange were ahead 51–47 with 9:00 left in the game. Syracuse clung to its lead until 3:50 was left, when Hollis Thompson sank a three-pointer to tie the game at 55–55 and begin what turned out to be a decisive 9–0 Georgetown run that put the Hoyas ahead 61–55 with 2:08 remaining. Georgetown went on to win 64–56, having held the Orange to 39.6 shooting from the field and 4-for-16 (25%) in three-pointers. It was John Thompson III's first win at the [[Carrier Dome]] in six tries, and the Orange's third straight home less, only the third time that had happened in [[Jim Boeheim]]′s 35-year tenure as Syracuse's head coach.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052759/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310400183 Anonymous, "No. 11 Georgetown takes control in final four minutes to beat No. 13 Syracuse," Associated Press, February 9, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310400183 espn.com Georgetown vs. Syracuse –  Box Score – February 9, 2011 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=310400183 espn.com Georgetown vs. Syracuse –  Play-by-Play – February 9, 2011 – ESPN]</ref> Four days later, Georgetown extended its winning streak to eight – the Hoyas's longest conference winning streak since the [[2006-07 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2006–07 season]] –  and won its 20th game of the season, coming from behind to defeat [[2010–11 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]] at the Verizon Center in a match-up of the two top-shooting teams in the Big East. Austin Freeman injured his ankle with 1:13 left in the first half of the game against the Golden Eagles, but returned in the second half and played through pain to finish with 17 points. Chris Wright had 20 points, and Hollis Thompson pulled down a career-high 13 rebounds.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052936/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310440046 Anonymous, "Georgetown overcomes long-range slump for eighth straight win," Associated Press, February 13, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310440046 espn.com Marquette vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – February 13, 2011 – ESPN]</ref>

In third place in the Big East and rising to No. 9 in the AP Poll, the Hoyas went on the road to play another ranked team, No. 12 [[2010–11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]], three days later. The Hoyas led 37–36 at the half and 70–69 with 4:01 left in the game, but did not score again as Connecticut finished the game with nine unanswered points, and the Huskies upset the Hoyas 78–70. Chris Wright led the Hoyas with 19 points, while Jason Clark had 13 and Austin Freeman 12, and Hollis Thompson came off the bench to score 10.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202053107/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310470041 Anonymous, "Kemba Walker, No. 12 Connecticut end No. 9 Georgetown's 8-game win streak," Associated Press, February 17, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310470041 espn.com Georgetown vs. Connecticut –  Box Score – February 16, 2011 – ESPN]</ref> With their eight-game winning streak broken, the Hoyas visited [[2010–11 South Florida Bulls men's basketball team|South Florida]] and beat the Bulls behind Chris Wright's season-high 26 points, including 8-for-8 from the free-throw line and six free throws in the final 29.7 seconds of play, and 10 points by Jason Clark.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202102724/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310500058 Anonymous, "Georgetown rebounds from loss by holding off South Florida," Associated Press, February 19, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310500058 espn.com Georgetown vs. South Florida  –  Box Score – February 19, 2011 – ESPN]</ref> It turned out to be Georgetown's last victory of the season.

Georgetown had fallen to No. 11 in the AP Poll when its season-ending losing streak began at the Verizon Center with an upset loss to [[2010–11 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]], breaking the Bearcats′ 20-game losing streak on the road to ranked teams that dated back to January 14, 2004. Although Austin Freeman scored 19 points, the Hoyas shot 25 percent from the field as a team, their worst shooting performance since at least the [[1996-97 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1996–97 season]]. Bigger than the loss of the game was the loss of Chris Wright, who left the game with a broken hand with 15:53 left to play.<ref>[http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId/310540046 Anonymous, "Cincinnati upsets No. 11 Georgetown for rare Big East road win," Associated Press, February 24, 2011.]{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310540046 espn.com Cincinnati vs. Georgetown  –  Box Score – February 23, 2011 – ESPN]</ref> Wright was unable to play – breaking his 93-game collegiate starting streak – when Georgetown hosted No. 17 Syracuse in a rematch with former [[President of the United States|President]] [[Bill Clinton]], former Georgetown and [[National Basketball Association]] star [[Alonzo Mourning]], and [[Washington Capitals]] and [[Washington Wizards]] owner [[Ted Leonsis]] looking on. Syracuse was ahead for almost the entire first half, finishing with a 9–2 run that gave the Orange a 33–23 lead at halftime. Georgetown battled back in the second half to take a 45–43 lead with 10:00 left to play, but from there Syracuse outscored the Hoyas 15–6 for a 58–51 upset win. Austin Freeman had 16 points and Jason Clark scored 11.<ref name=ap20110227>[http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId/310570046 Anonymous, "Hoyas fall without Chris Wright as Orange win 4th straight," Associated Press, February 27, 2011.]{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310570046 espn.com Syracuse vs. Georgetown  –  Box Score – February 26, 2011 – ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=310570046 espn.com Syracuse vs. Georgetown  –  Play-by-Play – February 26, 2011 – ESPN]</ref> With Wright – who had undergone surgery on his hand – still out and the Hoyas falling to No. 17 in the AP Poll, the season ended with a loss at Cincinnati, in which Freeman alone provided most of Georgetown's offense, playing 37 minutes and scoring 21 points. Both teams were shooting only 33 percent from the floor with 10 minutes left to play, and Georgetown, although leading the Big East with a team field goal percentage of 48.5, shot only 32 percent from the field against Cincinnati. Hollis Thompson had 12 points.<ref name=ap20110305>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202102716/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310642132 Anonymous, "Cincinnati pads March resume by rolling No. 17 Georgetown," Associated Press, March 5, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310642132 espn.com Georgetown vs. Cincinnati –  Box Score – March 5, 2011 – ESPN]</ref>

===Big East tournament===
{{main|2011 Big East men's basketball tournament}}

Georgetown finished the regular season in eighth place in the Big East with a 10–8 conference record. As the number eight seed in the [[2011 Big East men's basketball tournament|2011 Big East tournament]], the Hoyas earned a bye in the first round. In the second round – now ranked No. 22 in the AP Poll after their season-ending losing streak – they faced the ninth seed, No. 21 Connecticut. Like Georgetown, the Huskies had struggled late in the regular season, losing four of their final five games, but they had defeated 16th-seed DePaul the previous day in the first round of the tournament to advance to face the Hoyas. Chris Wright's injured hand forced him to sit out again. The game was tied at 15–15 halfway through the first half, but with Georgetown in early foul trouble, Connecticut embarked on a 22–7 run to take a 37–22 advantage with 3:36 left in the first half, and the Huskies led 42–30 at halftime. With the Georgetown backcourt shooting a combined 2-for-13 (15.4%), Julian Vaugh held scoreless, and Connecticut junior guard [[Kemba Walker]] scoring 28 points, the Huskies cruised through the second half to knock Georgetown out of the tournament with a 79–62 win. Jason Clark led the Hoyas with 23 points, Austin Freeman had 20, and Hollis Thompson scored 10.<ref name=ap20110310>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052757/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310680046 Anonymous, "Huskies roll past Hoyas to stay alive in Big East tourney," Associated Press, March 10, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310680046 espn.com Connecticut vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – March 9, 2011 – ESPN]</ref>

===NCAA tournament===
{{main|2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament}}

Losers of four straight, No. 22 Georgetown nonetheless had a 21–10 record that was good enough to earn the Hoyas a bid in the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2011 NCAA tournament]], their second consecutive appearance in the tournament and fifth in six seasons. Seeded sixth in the Southwest Region, in the Round of 64 – termed the "Second Round" of the tournament that year – they met 11th-seeded [[2010–11 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]], which had lost five of its last eight games prior to the tournament but had defeated [[2010–11 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] in the "First Four" round to advance to play the Hoyas. Chris Wright finally returned to play, raising hopes that the Hoyas could pull out of their slump and make a run in the tournament, but Wright shot 3-for-13 and finished with only six points. The Hoyas led 19–18 with 7:48 left in the first half, but the Rams then went on a 9–0 run to take a lead they never relinquished. VCU led 35–24 at halftime, and in the second half continued to extend their lead, beginning with a 14–4 run that put them ahead 49–28 with about 15 minutes left to play. Georgetown closed to 49–34 with 13:51 remaining, but never threatened the Rams′ lead. The Hoyas committed 17 turnovers against only six for the Rams, and shot only 5-for-26 (19.2%) from three-point range — with Freeman, Wright, and Clark combining for 0-for-16 in three-point attempts – while VCU made 12 of 25 attempted three-pointers (48.0%). Despite 26 points off the bench by Hollis Thompson and 10 points by Austin Freeman, VCU went on to win 74–56 in a shocking upset, dealing the Hoyas their most lopsided NCAA tournament defeat since an 86–62 loss to [[1995–96 UMass Minutemen basketball team|Massachusetts]] in [[1996 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1996]]. It was the first time VCU had ever won more than one game in an NCAA tournament, and the Rams went all the way to the [[Final Four]] before they were eliminated. For the Hoyas, it was their third straight NCAA tournament elimination in the tournament's first weekend, and the second consecutive year that they had been knocked out in their first game.<ref name=ap20110318>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052707/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=310770046 Anonymous, "Sharpshooting VCU shocks Georgetown for second win of tournament," Associated Press, March 19, 2011.]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=310770046 espn.com VCU vs. Georgetown –  Box Score – March 18, 2011 – ESPN]</ref>

===Wrap-up===

Starting all 32 games, Austin Freeman finished the season with a team-leading 17.6 points per game, having shot 47.6 percent from the field and a team-best 87.0 percent from the free-throw line. Chris Wright, who missed three late games because of his hand injury, started in all 29 of his appearances and scored 12.9 points per game – second best on the team – on 41.4 percent shooting from the field and 78.3 percent in free throws. Jason Clark, starting every game, finished with a field-goal percentage of 48.3, a free-throw percentage of 77.0, and 12.0 points per game. Shooting 51.9 percent from three-point range – best on the team – Hollis Thompson appeared in all 32 games, starting 22 of them, and also had a team-best 51.9 percent average in field goals overall and averaged 8.6 points per game. Julian Vaughn, who missed one game but started the other 31, was second-best for the season in field goal percentage at 49.4 and averaged 7.8 points, and he led the Hyas with 6.1 rebounds per game. Other players seeing significant playing time were Jerrelle Benimon, Nate Lubick, and Henry Sims, all of whom played in every game, and Markel Starks, who saw action in 30 games. Lubick started in 13 of his appearances, while Sims started one game.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/georgetown/2011.html sports-reference.com 2010-11 Georgetown Hoyas Roster and Stats]</ref>

After the season, a major turnover occurred on Georgetown's roster. Mainstays Austin Freeman, Julian Vaughn, and Chris Wright all graduated in 2011, as did reserve guard Ryan Dougherty. Freeman left after a 129-game collegiate career in which he had started 117 times, shot 49.8 percent from the field, and averaged 13.7 points per game.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/austin-freeman-1.html sports-reference.com Austin Freeman]</ref> In his 110 games, 94 of them starts, Wright had averaged 12.4 points per game on 45.9 percent shooting from the field,<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/chris-wright-2.html sports-reference.com Chris Wright]</ref> while Vaughn completed his career after a freshman year at [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] and three years at Georgetown with a combined 126 games played (95 at Georgetown), 72 starts (65 at Georgetown), and 5.1 points per game with a 52.5 percent field-goal percentage, although during his three years at Georgetown he averaged 5.8 points per game on 52.7 percent shooting.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/julian-vaughn-1.html sports-reference.com Julian Vaughn]</ref> Freeman, Vaughn, and Wright all went undrafted in the [[2011 NBA draft]]; all three played professional basketball overseas and, during a three-day stint with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in [[2012–13 Dallas Mavericks season|March 2013]], Wright became the first person to play in the [[National Basketball Association]] after being diagnosed with [[multiple sclerosis]].

On May 19, 2011, sophomore guard Vee Sanford announced that he was transferring to [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]], where, after fulfilling a requirement to sit out the [[2011–12 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|2011–12 season]], he could begin play with the Flyers in [[2012–13 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|2012–13]] with two years of college eligibility remaining.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/186722-ex-georgetown-guard-to-transfer-to-dayton |title=Anonymous, "Ex-Georgetown guard to transfer to Dayton," sportingnews.com, May 19, 2011. |access-date=December 1, 2017 |archive-date=December 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171202053330/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/186722-ex-georgetown-guard-to-transfer-to-dayton |url-status=dead }}</ref> Sanford became the eleventh Hoya player in six seasons to leave Georgetown prior to the expiration of his college eligibility. Hollis Thompson initially declared for the [[2011 NBA draft]], indicating that he planned to forego his final two years of college eligibility, but he never hired an agent and instead returned to school to play for Georgetown [[2011–12 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the following season]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7744507/georgetown-hoyas-hollis-thompson-enter-2012-nba-draft Anonymous, "Hollis Thompson to enter draft," Associated Press, March 27, 2012.]</ref>

Although among the top-shooting teams in the United States during the season, the Hoyas had finished the year with a five-game losing streak. They clearly missed the injured Chris Wright during that stretch,<ref name=ap20110227/><ref name=ap20110305/><ref name=ap20110310/> but their backcourt also slumped in the final games of the year, especially from three-point range,<ref name=ap20110227/><ref name=ap20110305/><ref name=ap20110310/><ref name=ap20110318/> and that had torpedoed their hopes of advancing in both the Big East tournament and the NCAA tournament. The season also ended in a sloppy, off-target performance against VCU,<ref name=ap20110318/> a loss which left Georgetown with no NCAA tournament victories since the first game of the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2008 tournament]] despite three appearances in four years over that stretch. It continued a troubling pattern established since their Final Four appearance in [[2007 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2007]] of early upsets in the NCAA tournament at the hands of decided underdogs.<ref name=ap20110318/> That pattern would continue [[2011-12 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the following season]].

The 2010–11 Hoyas finished with a record of 21–11. In the Top 25 of the AP Poll all season, they finished the year ranked No. 22 – their lowest rank of the year – in a final poll taken on March 7, before their losses in the Big East and NCAA tournaments. Although they had also been in the [[Coaches Poll]] Top 25 for almost the entire season, they finished the year unranked in that poll's postseason voting on March 29, which followed the two tournament losses.
